messages.author: Sayan Poddar
messages.body:
Dear AMBER developers and Users,
I was installing Amber22 and AmberTools23. Everything has gone smoothly but
when I executed *make test.serial,* some of the tests failed.
The very first line says
*Error: Could not import Amber Python modules!    Probably your Amber
Python environment was not set up correctly.*
I have added all this line in my .bashrc script
*export AMBERHOME=/home/sayan/software/amber/amber22*
*source /home/sayan/software/amber/amber22/amber.sh*
*test -f /home/sayan/software/amber/amber22/amber.sh  && source
/home/sayan/software/amber/amber22/amber.sh*
Also, echo $AMBERHOME and $PYTHONPATH showed the following lines.
*echo $AMBERHOME/home/sayan/software/amber/amber22echo $PYTHONPATH
/home/sayan/software/amber/amber22/lib/python3.12/site-packages:/home/sayan/software/amber/amber22/lib/python3.12/site-packages*
So, what else am I missing?
Thank you
-- 
*with regards*
*Sayan Poddar*
*PhD Research Scholar*
*Department of Biosciences and Biomedical Engineering*
*Indian Institute of Technology Indore*
*India*

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Tue, Mar 26, 2024, Sayan Poddar via AMBER wrote:
>
>I was installing Amber22 and AmberTools23. Everything has gone smoothly but
>when I executed *make test.serial,* some of the tests failed.
>
>*Error: Could not import Amber Python modules!    Probably your Amber
>Python environment was not set up correctly.*
Did you have -DDOWNLOAD_MINICONDA=TRUE in your run_cmake script?  What is
the result of typing "which python"?
...dac

messages.author: David A Case
messages.body:
On Fri, Mar 29, 2024, Sayan Poddar wrote:
>Yes run_cmake script has* -DDOWNLOAD_MINICONDA=TRUE*
>
>"which python" gives
>*/home/sayan/miniconda3/bin/python*
I'm running out of ideas here, so hope the python gurus can weigh in.
One final question: what is the result of 'python --version'.  If the python
in /home/sayan/miniconda3/bin is not version 3.12, that could conflict with
the python modules loaded in $AMBERHOME/lib/python3.12.
Also: look at the cmake log, and the output from "make install" to see if
there are any references to python that provide clues.
...dac

messages.author: Todd Minehardt
messages.body:
Sayan,
The issue is with python versions > 3.10.x.
See
http://archive.ambermd.org/202402/0027.html
and search the archive from
about Oct 2023 to present for more info; but the net of it is go with
python version < 3.11.x.
Cheers,
Todd
